```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(peacesciencer)
library(broom)
library(marginaleffects)

conflict_df <- create_stateyears(system = 'gw') |>
  filter(year %in% c(1946:1999)) |>
  add_ucdp_acd(type = c("intrastate"), only_wars = FALSE) |>
  add_democracy() |>
  add_creg_fractionalization() |>
  add_sdp_gdp() |>
  add_rugged_terrain()

bivariate_model <- glm(ucdponset ~ wbgdppc2011est,
                       data = conflict_df, family = "binomial")

b0 <- round(coef(bivariate_model)[["(Intercept)"]], 2)
b1 <- round(coef(bivariate_model)[["wbgdppc2011est"]], 2)
b1_fmt <- ifelse(b1 >= 0, paste0("+ ", b1), paste0("- ", abs(b1)))
or_b1 <- round(exp(b1), 2)
pct_change_b1 <- round((1 - exp(b1)) * 100, 1)
logodds_9 <- round(b0 + b1 * 9, 2)
odds_9 <- round(exp(logodds_9), 3)
odds_9_plus_1 <- round(1 + odds_9, 3)
prob_9 <- round(odds_9 / (1 + odds_9), 4)
```

# Interpreting Logistic Regression

## The Model Equation

<br>

$$\log\left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right) = `r b0` `r b1_fmt` \times \text{logGDPpc}$$

## What Are Log-Odds?

<br>

::: {.incremental}
- Logistic regression coefficients are on the **log-odds** scale
- The **direction** of the effect is easy to read: positive = more likely, negative = less likely
- But the **magnitude** is hard to interpret directly
- We need to transform the coefficients into something more intuitive
:::

## Odds Ratios

<br>

- **Exponentiate** the coefficient to get the **odds ratio**
- For each one-unit increase in the predictor, the odds of the outcome are **multiplied** by the odds ratio

$$OR = e^b$$

## Interpreting the Odds Ratio {.smaller}

<br>

$$\log\left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right) = `r b0` `r b1_fmt` \times \text{logGDPpc}$$

<br>

$e^{`r b1`} \approx `r or_b1`$

<br>

For each one-unit increase in log GDP per capita, the odds of conflict onset are **multiplied by `r or_b1`** — a **`r pct_change_b1`% decrease** in the odds of conflict onset.

## Calculating Odds Ratios in R {.smaller}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: odds_ratios
#| echo: true

tidy(bivariate_model, exponentiate = TRUE) |>
  select(term, estimate, p.value)
```

## Predicted Probabilities by Hand

<br>

Probability of conflict onset for a country with log GDP per capita of 9 (~$8,000):

$$\log\left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right) = `r b0` `r b1_fmt` \times 9 = `r logodds_9`$$

$$\frac{p}{1-p} = e^{`r logodds_9`} = `r odds_9` \quad \Rightarrow \quad p = \frac{`r odds_9`}{`r odds_9_plus_1`} \approx `r prob_9`$$

## Predicted Probabilities with `marginaleffects`

```{r}
#| label: pred_probs
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true

prediction_data <- data.frame(wbgdppc2011est = c(6, 7, 8, 9, 10))
pred_results <- predictions(bivariate_model, newdata = prediction_data)

tidy(pred_results) |>
  select(wbgdppc2011est, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |>
  mutate(GDP_approx = paste0("~$", round(exp(wbgdppc2011est))))
```

## Visualizing Predicted Probabilities

```{r}
#| label: plot_predictions
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

plot_predictions(bivariate_model, condition = "wbgdppc2011est") +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Probability of Conflict Onset",
    x = "Log GDP per capita",
    y = "Pr(Conflict Onset)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Multiple Logistic Regression

## Multiple Logistic Regression

<br>

::: {.incremental}
- Just as with linear models, we can also run multiple logistic regressions
- We can include multiple predictors in the model
- Usually we want to include our main predictor of interest and control variables
- The interpretation of the coefficients is the same as in the bivariate models
:::

## 

<br>

Download the data using the `peacesciencer` package if you haven't already...

<br>

```{r}
#| label: conflict_df
#| echo: true

conflict_df <- create_stateyears(system = 'gw') |>
  filter(year %in% c(1946:1999)) |>
  add_ucdp_acd(type=c("intrastate"), only_wars = FALSE) |>
  add_democracy() |>
  add_creg_fractionalization() |>
  add_sdp_gdp() |>
  add_rugged_terrain()
```

## 

<br>

Example, including multiple predictors associated with conflict:

```{r}
#| label: multivariate_model
#| echo: true

conflict_model <- glm(ucdponset ~ ethfrac + relfrac + v2x_polyarchy + 
                          rugged + wbgdppc2011est + wbpopest,
                  data= conflict_df,
                  family = "binomial")

summary(conflict_model)
```

## Predicted Probabilities

<br>

```{r}
#| label: marginal_effects
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

# select some countries for a given year
selected_countries <- conflict_df |>
  filter(
    gw_name %in% c("United States of America", "Venezuela", "Rwanda"),
    year == 1999)

# calculate margins for the subset
marg_effects <- predictions(conflict_model, newdata = selected_countries)

# tidy the results
library(broom)

tidy(marg_effects) |>
  select(gw_name, estimate, p.value, conf.low, conf.high) 
```

# Regression Tables

## What's in a Regression Table?

![](images/fearon_laitin.png){fig-align=center}

## Regression Tables with `modelsummary`

<br>

::: {.incremental}
- Oftentimes we want to show multiple models at once (like F&L)
- We want to compare across them and see which is the best model
- How can we do that? 
- There are **many** ways to do this in R
- We will use the `modelsummary` package
:::

## Run Multiple Models

<br>

```{r}
#| label: multiple_models
#| echo: true

ethnicity <- glm(ucdponset ~ ethfrac + relfrac + wbgdppc2011est + wbpopest, # store each model in an object
                  data = conflict_df,
                  family = "binomial")

democracy <- glm(ucdponset ~ v2x_polyarchy + wbgdppc2011est +  wbpopest,
                  data = conflict_df,
                  family = "binomial")

terrain <- glm(ucdponset ~ rugged + wbgdppc2011est + wbpopest ,
                  data = conflict_df,
                  family = "binomial")

full_model <- glm(ucdponset ~ ethfrac + relfrac + v2x_polyarchy + rugged +
                        wbgdppc2011est + wbpopest,
                  data = conflict_df,
                  family = "binomial")
```


## Prep Data for Display

<br>

```{r}
#| label: prep_data
#| echo: true

models <- list("Ethnicity" = ethnicity,  # store list of models in an object
               "Democracy" = democracy, 
               "Terrain" = terrain, 
               "Full Model" = full_model)

coef_map <- c("ethfrac" = "Ethnic Frac",  # map coefficients
        "relfrac" = "Religions Frac",     #(change names and order)
        "v2x_polyarchy" = "Polyarchy",
        "rugged" = "Terrain",
        "wbgdppc2011est" = "Per capita GDP",
        "wbpopest" = "Population",
        "(Intercept)" = "Intercept")

caption = "Table 1: Predictors of Conflict Onset" # store caption
reference = "See appendix for data sources."      # store reference notes
```

## Display the Models {.smaller}

```{r}
#| label: display_models

library(modelsummary)

modelsummary(models,                      # display the table
             stars = TRUE,                # include stars for significance
             gof_map = c("nobs"),         # goodness of fit stats to include   
             coef_map = coef_map,         # coefficient mapping
             title = caption,             # title
             notes = reference)           # source note
```

# Coefficient Plots

## {.smaller}

<br> 

This don't look too good...

```{r}
#| label: bad_regression_table
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

modelsummary(conflict_model, 
             stars = TRUE,  
             gof_map = c("nobs"),
             coef_map = coef_map,
             title = caption, 
             notes = reference)
```

## 

<br> 

So we can use `ggplot` to make a coefficient plot instead...

```{r}
#| label: coef_plot
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

library(ggplot2)

modelplot(conflict_model, 
          coef_map = rev(coef_map), # rev() reverses list order
          coef_omit = "Intercept", 
          color = "blue") + # use plus to add customizations like any ggplot object
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = .75) + # red 0 line
  labs(
    title = "Figure 1: Predictors of Conflict Onset",
    caption = "See appendix for data sources."
  ) 
```
